author: Breyer
authority: Chief Justice Stone-Zsela, a member of the judgment coalition, assigns this lead opinion.
form: Form fixed before assignment or counts: one signed lead opinion of the Court after plenary merits submission, with Parts I–V separating genuine jurisdictional, constitutional and remedial questions and their distinct coalitions. Six Associates can carry every part, so there is no basis to divide authorship. Stone's partial concurrence and the Scalia–Thomas partial dissent perform distinct legal work; no judgment-only coalition is falsely described as a full join.
reason: Breyer's supported Troxel approach fits the distinction between actual parent-authorized care and an independent grandparent entitlement, while his accepted passage rule preserves workable ordinary regulation. The opinion also keeps the entered monetary award separate from prospective jurisdiction. The six full joiners have already settled those grounds; no formulation objection requires expansion. Stevens is the strongest pool alternative for the collateral-jurisdiction and innocent-presence questions, but Breyer can carry that work with the lower count. Stone's partial join cannot support authorship of the full opinion, and the form is not divided to alter eligibility.
